label: OpenMetadata
description: Open-source metadata management platform. Centralise data discovery, lineage, data quality and governance across your Hadoop and cloud-native data stack.

openshiftScc.comment: Grant anyuid ONLY to the SAs whose images pin a UID/GID or run as root: the bundled OpenSearch (uses the namespace 'default' SA, hardcodes fsGroup:1000/runAsUser) and every Airflow component/job (uid 50000) — INCLUDING the migrate-database-job and create-user-job SAs (their pods run the airflow image as uid 50000 and are what apply/seed the metadata DB; miss them and the DB never migrates -> app pods hang on wait-for-airflow-migrations). The OpenMetadata server SA ('{{releaseName}}') and both postgres SAs are intentionally EXCLUDED so they keep restricted-v2 — the server pods set runAsNonRoot with no UID and need the platform to inject one, which anyuid would suppress. Airflow SA names are {{releaseName}}-airflow-<component> and need not exist yet (RBAC binds by name).

endpoints.label: OpenMetadata UI
endpoints.description: Data discovery, lineage and governance portal

variables.comment: 'true' while the 'Enable Ranger TagSync' switch is off. Declared after rangerTagSyncEnabled, which it reads.
variables.name: rangerTagSyncDisabled

variables.comment: The release's current chart value: on an upgrade the deployed values are part of the form state, on a first install it is unset.
variables.name: rangerTagSyncDeployedEnabled

bindings.name: om-fullname-pin
bindings._description: Names the chart's Service, Deployment and ServiceAccount exactly like the release. Without it the chart names them '<release>-openmetadata' unless the release name already contains 'openmetadata', and KDPS's post-install steps (base ingestion, Atlas federation, Ranger TagSync) and the endpoint it shows address the Service by the release name. The server sets the same value (releaseNameValues) for the deploys that do not go through the wizard.

bindings.name: ingress-setup
bindings._description: Writes the canonical ingress shape every KDPS chart accepts. The `hosts[]` entry uses the rich object form `{host, paths[]}` so OpenMetadata- and Trino-style charts work out of the box; the Superset chart's template was made shape-tolerant (accepts string OR object) in chart >= 0.12.25.

bindings.name: openshift-route-allowlist
bindings._description: On OpenShift the chart copies ingress.annotations onto its Route; some clusters refuse a Route without this router annotation.

bindings.name: ingress-nginx-tuning
bindings._description: Backslash-escaped dots in the leaf key — the UI binding engine (bindings.ts:pathToParts) treats backslash-dot as a literal dot so the rendered values look like `ingress.annotations: { "nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size": "..." }`.

bindings.comment: Plain Kubernetes: label the ServiceMonitor for the kube-prometheus-stack release that should scrape it, plus the labels its Prometheus selects by (found by discovery). The chart always creates the ServiceMonitor in the release namespace. Gated on isVanillaK8s as well, so an OpenShift ServiceMonitor never gets the kube-prometheus 'release' label, even though the hidden Monitoring group keeps its default release name.
bindings.name: service-monitor-enable

bindings.comment: OpenShift: the self-managed kube-prometheus-stack is skipped (dependency skipOnOpenShift), so the platform's user-workload monitoring scrapes OpenMetadata instead. The Monitoring group, 'Expose ServiceMonitor' included, is hidden on OpenShift, so serviceMonitor.enabled is forced here. The chart then creates the ServiceMonitor (port admin, path /prometheus) in the release namespace, which is the project user-workload monitoring reads and the one the deploy preflight checks the account may write to. It carries no kube-prometheus 'release' label, because 'service-monitor-enable' is gated on isVanillaK8s. Gated on isOpenShift so vanilla k8s is unaffected.
bindings.name: service-monitor-openshift

bindings.comment: OpenShift: disable OpenSearch's vm.max_map_count sysctl init container. It runs PRIVILEGED as root, which even the anyuid SCC (granted by the deploy preflight) does not permit — only the privileged SCC would, which we don't want to require. OpenSearch here is singleNode (discovery.type=single-node), so bootstrap checks are skipped and a low max_map_count is a harmless warning rather than a startup failure. Gated on isOpenShift so vanilla k8s keeps the sysctl init.
bindings.name: opensearch-sysctl-off-openshift

bindings.comment: OpenMetadata API address handed to Ranger TagSync, derived from the ingress host. Only with the switch on: the post-install registration reads it, and a release with TagSync off must not carry one.
bindings.name: ranger-tagsync-endpoint-from-ingress

bindings.comment: Operator override of the address above. Declared after it so that it wins; skipped when blank so the derived address stays.
bindings.name: ranger-tagsync-endpoint-override

bindings.comment: Each optional target is skipped when its field is blank, so a blank field never overwrites a value (the chart default, the deployed value, or the Trino mapping KDPS writes for Trino base ingestion).
bindings.name: ranger-tagsync-config

bindings.comment: Switch turned off on a release that has TagSync on (an upgrade: the deployed values are in the form state). Writes false explicitly, or the deployed true would be re-sent. A first install with the switch off gets no ranger.tagSync value at all.
bindings.name: ranger-tagsync-off
base-hive-ingestion-toggle
bindings._description: Base Hive ingestion requires Airflow → also flips dependencies.enabled when the operator turns this on (same pattern as atlas-federation-toggle).

bindings.name: base-trino-ingestion-toggle
bindings._description: Base Trino ingestion requires Airflow too → flips dependencies.enabled when turned on (same pattern as the Hive toggle).

bindings.name: atlas-federation-toggle
bindings._description: Atlas federation requires Airflow → also flips dependencies.enabled when the operator turns this on. Express via two targets so the bindings engine sets both atomically.

bindings.name: atlas-url-discovered
bindings._description: Sets atlasFederation.hostPort from the Ambari-discovered Atlas service.

bindings.name: atlas-url-override
bindings._description: Override the discovered Atlas URL when the operator types in the override field.

fields.name: runAsUser
fields.label: Run pods as a specific UID (optional)
fields.help: Leave blank: OpenShift picks a UID from the project's range.
fields.helpMore: Set a UID only if you must pin one. It must fall inside the namespace's openshift.io/sa.scc.uid-range annotation, or admission rejects the pods.

form.name: externalOpensearchOptions
form.label: External OpenSearch (OpenShift)
form.help: On OpenShift, point OpenMetadata at an external OpenSearch.
form.helpMore:
The bundled OpenSearch needs root and privileged init containers (vm.max_map_count) that OpenShift's restricted-v2 SCC rejects. Entering a host below turns it off.
The chart connects over plain host:port, without credentials or a custom CA: use an unauthenticated endpoint or an in-cluster Service.

fields.name: externalOpensearch.host
fields.label: OpenSearch host
fields.help: Host or in-cluster Service of the external OpenSearch. Blank: the bundled one.
fields.helpMore: e.g. opensearch.search.svc.cluster.local. The bundled OpenSearch does not start under OpenShift's restricted-v2 SCC.

fields.name: externalOpensearch.port
fields.label: Port
fields.help: External OpenSearch port (default 9200).

fields.name: externalOpensearch.scheme
fields.label: Scheme
fields.help: http or https.
fields.helpMore: https with a private CA is not supported yet.

form.name: releaseName
form.label: Release Name
form.validationHint: Use at most 53 lower-case letters, digits, '-' and '.', starting and ending with a letter or digit (Helm's rule for release names).

form.name: namespace
form.label: Namespace Kubernetes
form.validationHint: Namespace too long — the Kerberos principal (oma-ing-<namespace>) would exceed the 32-character IPA limit.

fields.name: security.adminUsers
fields.label: Admin users (comma-separated)
fields.help: User names given the OpenMetadata Admin role, comma separated.
fields.helpMore: OpenMetadata grants Admin by user name only, not by group: list each administrator.

fields.name: security.principalDomain
fields.label: Admin email domain
fields.help: Email domain of the admin users, as your identity provider issues it.
fields.helpMore: Filled from the security profile (oidc.principalDomain). Blank with no profile value, OpenMetadata uses open-metadata.org, and the first OIDC login fails with 'Account already exists' when your domain differs.

form.name: authenticationConfig
form.label: Authentication
form.help: How users sign in: OIDC needs a Keycloak realm, LDAP a reachable directory.

fields.name: global.security.auth.mode
fields.label: Authentication mode
fields.help: Sets AUTHENTICATION_PROVIDER in the OpenMetadata server. Select 'oidc' to register a Keycloak client automatically.

fields.name: global.security.auth.oidc.providerName
fields.label: OIDC provider display name
fields.help: Label shown on the OpenMetadata login button (CUSTOM_OIDC_AUTHENTICATION_PROVIDER_NAME).

fields.name: global.security.auth.oidc.jwksUri
fields.label: JWKS URI override
fields.help: Leave blank for Keycloak; set only for another OIDC provider.
fields.helpMore: For Keycloak it is derived from the issuer: <issuer>/protocol/openid-connect/certs.

fields.name: global.security.auth.oidc.userClaim
fields.label: JWT user claim
fields.help: JWT claim used as the OpenMetadata username.

fields.name: global.security.auth.ldap.host
fields.label: LDAP host
fields.help: Hostname of the LDAP/AD server (without ldap:// prefix).

fields.name: global.security.auth.ldap.userBaseDn
fields.label: User search base DN
fields.help: Base DN for user lookup, e.g. ou=people,dc=example,dc=com.

fields.name: global.security.auth.ldap.userSearchFilter
fields.label: User search filter
fields.help: LDAP filter to locate a user. Use {0} as the username placeholder.

fields.name: global.security.auth.ldap.bindDn
fields.label: Bind DN (read account)
fields.help: Service account DN used to search the directory, e.g. cn=svc-om,ou=svc,dc=example,dc=com.

fields.name: global.security.auth.ldap.bindPassword
fields.label: Bind password
fields.help: Password for the bind DN.

fields.name: global.security.auth.ldap.groupBaseDn
fields.label: Group search base DN
fields.help: Base DN for group membership lookups (optional).

fields.name: global.security.auth.ldap.mailAttribute
fields.label: Email attribute
fields.help: LDAP attribute containing the user e-mail address.

fields.name: ui_trino_host
fields.label: Trino Coordinator
fields.help: Trino coordinator OpenMetadata reads metadata from.
fields.helpMore: With 'Enable Trino base ingestion', KDPS registers it in OpenMetadata as the Trino service trino-<release>.

fields.name: ui_trino_host_override
fields.label: Trino host:port (override)
fields.help: e.g. trino-coordinator.ns:8080 — overrides auto-discovered value.

form.name: ingestionConfig
form.label: Ingestion / Airflow (openmetadata-dependencies sub-chart)

fields.name: dependencies.enabled
fields.label: Deploy bundled Airflow
fields.help: Deploys the bundled Airflow. Turned on by Atlas federation and ingestion.

fields.name: dependencies.airflow.ingress.enabled
fields.label: Expose Airflow UI via ingress
fields.help: Expose the Airflow UI to browse pipeline runs.
fields.helpMore: Its host is the OpenMetadata host with an -airflow suffix. Off, Airflow is reachable from OpenMetadata only.

fields.name: dependencies.airflow.logs.persistence.enabled
fields.label: Persist Airflow logs (requires RWX storage)
fields.help: Keep Airflow logs on a shared volume. Needs ReadWriteMany storage.
fields.helpMore:
Off, each Airflow pod keeps its logs in its own temporary volume, enough for tests.
On, the chart creates a ReadWriteMany volume (NFS, EFS, CephFS…). local-path does not support it: on such a cluster, give a volume you created under 'Existing PVC'.

fields.name: dependencies.airflow.logs.persistence.size
fields.label: Log PVC size
fields.help: Size of the shared log volume the chart creates.
fields.helpMore: Used only when no existing PVC is given.

fields.name: dependencies.airflow.logs.persistence.storageClassName
fields.label: Storage class (must support RWX)
fields.help: Storage class supporting ReadWriteMany. Blank: the default.
fields.helpMore: e.g. nfs-csi, efs-sc, rook-cephfs, longhorn. Leave it blank only if the cluster's default supports ReadWriteMany; local-path does not, and the volume stays Pending.

fields.name: dependencies.airflow.logs.persistence.existingClaim
fields.label: Existing PVC name (optional)
fields.help: A volume claim you created, used instead of a new one.
fields.helpMore: In the release namespace. Size and storage class above are then ignored.

form.help: Airflow and the ingestion runner, needed by every OpenMetadata pipeline.
form.helpMore: Atlas federation and Trino or Hive ingestion run there. Turn it off only to use an external Airflow.

form.name: atlasFederation
form.label: Atlas Federation
form.help: Brings the context's Atlas catalog into OpenMetadata.
form.helpMore: Creates the Atlas and database services and a scheduled ingestion pipeline; needs the bundled Airflow. OpenMetadata signs in to Atlas with a user name and password: Atlas's file users, or an LDAP service account given in a Secret.

fields.name: atlasFederation.enabled
fields.label: Enable Atlas federation
fields.help: Federate the platform context's Atlas into OpenMetadata.
fields.helpMore: KDPS creates the federation user, grants it read access (Ranger or Atlas simple authorization) and registers the Atlas service and its pipeline. Everything comes from the platform context.

fields.name: atlasFederation.existingSecret
fields.label: Existing Secret (service account)
fields.help: Secret with 'username' and 'password' of the account used for Atlas.
fields.helpMore:
Optional, in the release namespace. Required when Atlas signs users in against LDAP: use an existing LDAP service account; nothing is changed in Atlas.
With Ranger, KDPS grants the account read access; with Atlas simple authorization, add it to atlas-simple-authz-policy.json yourself.
Blank: KDPS creates and manages the account. The Secret may be created by the install itself, e.g. by external-secrets.

fields.name: atlasFederation.allowFileAuth
fields.label: Allow Atlas file authentication
fields.help: Lets KDPS turn on Atlas file authentication to create OpenMetadata's user.
fields.helpMore: Only for an Atlas with no file users and no LDAP account given above (e.g. Kerberos only). Warning: file authentication also adds a local Atlas administrator, a password way in next to Kerberos or LDAP. Off, the deploy stops with a message instead of changing Atlas.

fields.name: atlasFederation.schedule
fields.label: Ingestion schedule (cron)
fields.help: Default every 6h.

fields.name: atlasFederation.databaseServiceNames
fields.label: Target OM database services
fields.help: OpenMetadata services that receive Atlas tables. Blank: the Hive ingestion's.
fields.helpMore: Comma separated. Blank follows the Hive base ingestion service of this release.

form.name: baseIngestion
form.label: Base Metadata Ingestion (Hive / Trino)
form.help: Ingests Hive and Trino table metadata directly into OpenMetadata.
form.helpMore: It creates the database services and their tables; Atlas federation then adds Atlas lineage and tags to them. Turns the bundled Airflow on.

fields.name: baseIngestion.hiveEnabled
fields.label: Enable Hive base ingestion
fields.help: Ingest table metadata from the context's HiveServer2 on a schedule.
fields.helpMore: Turn it on together with Atlas federation to federate Atlas and Hive.

fields.name: baseIngestion.hiveServiceName
fields.label: OM database service name
fields.help: Name of the OpenMetadata Hive service. Blank: hive-<cluster>.
fields.helpMore: Atlas federation's target services follow it when left blank.

fields.name: baseIngestion.hiveHostPort
fields.label: HiveServer2 host:port
fields.help: From the platform context. Override only to use another HiveServer2.
fields.helpMore: On an external context without Ambari, enter it here.

fields.name: baseIngestion.hiveScheme
fields.label: Connection scheme
fields.help: From the platform context. Override only to force a scheme.
fields.helpMore: hive+https, hive+http or hive, from the context's transport mode and SSL setting.

externalFields.name: baseIngestion.hiveUseSSL
externalFields.label: Use TLS
externalFields.help: hive.server2.use.SSL — with HTTP transport this yields hive+https.

fields.name: baseIngestion.hiveAuthMode
fields.label: Authentication
fields.help: From the platform context. Override only to force it.
fields.helpMore: kerberos uses SPNEGO with the keytab Airflow renews.

fields.name: baseIngestion.hiveKerberosServiceName
fields.label: Kerberos service name
fields.help: SPN service name for HiveServer2 (usually 'hive'). Used only when authentication is kerberos.

fields.name: baseIngestion.hiveUsername
fields.label: Username (ldap/basic)
fields.help: Used only when authentication is ldap or basic.

fields.name: baseIngestion.hivePassword
fields.label: Password (ldap/basic)
fields.help: Used only when authentication is ldap or basic.

fields.name: baseIngestion.hiveSchedule
fields.label: Ingestion schedule (cron)
fields.help: Default every 12h.

fields.name: baseIngestion.hiveSchemaIncludes
fields.label: Schema include patterns
fields.help: Optional comma-separated regex patterns of schemas/databases to include (e.g. odp_functional_tests). Blank ingests all schemas.

fields.name: hive.externalKeytabSecret
fields.label: External ingestion service keytab Secret
fields.help: Secret with the ingestion keytab from another realm. Blank: KDPS issues it.
fields.helpMore:
Only for an external context whose KDC KDPS cannot reach (no KDC account on the context). Key 'service.keytab'; the principal is read from it. It serves all federated ingestion: Hive, Atlas, HDFS.
kubectl -n <ns> create secret generic om-keytab --from-file=service.keytab=./om-ingestion.keytab

fields.name: baseIngestion.trinoEnabled
fields.label: Enable Trino base ingestion
fields.help: Ingest the Trino coordinator above, so OpenMetadata tags reach Trino.
fields.helpMore: KDPS registers it as an OpenMetadata Trino service, signed in as the release's KDPS user over HTTPS (Trino chart 1.43.13+ with 'Let KDPS manage catalogs'), with a scheduled ingestion. Tags set in OpenMetadata then match Trino's resources in Ranger, and KDPS fills the TagSync mapping below. Turns the bundled Airflow on.

fields.name: baseIngestion.trinoServiceName
fields.label: OM database service name (Trino)
fields.help: Name of the OpenMetadata Trino service. Blank: trino-<release>.
fields.helpMore: It becomes the service whose tags Ranger TagSync syncs.

fields.name: baseIngestion.trinoSchedule
fields.label: Trino ingestion schedule (cron)
fields.help: Default every 12h.

fields.name: baseIngestion.trinoCatalogIncludes
fields.label: Catalog include patterns
fields.help: Optional comma-separated regex patterns of Trino catalogs to ingest (e.g. hive,iceberg). Blank ingests every catalog except 'system'.

fields.name: baseIngestion.trinoSchemaIncludes
fields.label: Schema include patterns (Trino)
fields.help: Optional comma-separated regex patterns of schemas to include. Blank ingests all schemas.

form.name: rangerTagSync
form.label: Ranger TagSync
form.help: Sends tags set in OpenMetadata to Ranger, enforced on Trino.
form.helpMore: OpenMetadata becomes a source of Ranger TagSync (RANGER-4978); its other sources, Atlas included, stay.

fields.name: rangerTagSyncEnabled
fields.label: Enable Ranger TagSync
fields.help: Registers OpenMetadata as a tag source of the platform's Ranger TagSync.
fields.helpMore:
Done after the install, then Ranger TagSync restarts once. Needs the bundled Airflow, an OpenMetadata address TagSync can reach, and an ingestion-bot token that expires (see below): until then the step is skipped with a warning.
On by default when the context exposes both Ranger and Atlas. Off, KDPS changes nothing in Ranger TagSync and only reports problems it sees there.

fields.name: rangerTagSyncToken
fields.label: OM bot JWT (optional — auto-fetched)
fields.help: Leave blank: KDPS reads the ingestion-bot token itself.
fields.helpMore:
It is stored as a password in Ranger TagSync's configuration (masked by Ambari, in a credential store on the host). KDPS only uses a token that expires: after the first install, regenerate the ingestion-bot token in OpenMetadata (Settings > Bots) with an expiry, e.g. 90 days.
That bot runs every ingestion pipeline: when its token expires, all ingestion stops. After each regeneration, run the release's 'Re-register …' actions so TagSync and the pipelines get the new token. KDPS warns 30 days before it expires.

fields.name: rangerTagSyncTokenSecretName
fields.label: Token Secret name (optional)
fields.help: K8s Secret holding the JWT under key 'tagsync-token'. Defaults to '<release>-tagsync-token' when empty.

fields.name: rangerTagSyncEndpoint
fields.label: OM API endpoint as seen from Ranger TagSync (optional)
fields.help: OpenMetadata API address Ranger TagSync uses. Blank: https://<ingress host>/api.
fields.helpMore: Set it when TagSync reaches OpenMetadata another way (DMZ, in-cluster Service).

fields.name: rangerTagSyncTrinoServiceFqn
fields.label: OM database service whose tags are synced
fields.help: OpenMetadata Trino service whose tags are synced.
fields.helpMore: With Trino base ingestion on, KDPS sets it to the service it registers and overrides this value. Without it, type the service name.

fields.name: rangerTagSyncRangerTrinoService
fields.label: Ranger service that receives the tags
fields.help: Ranger Trino service that receives the tags.
fields.helpMore: The Trino release's Ranger repository, <release>-<namespace> by default. With Trino base ingestion on, KDPS fills it. Blank without it: no mapping is written and Ranger rejects the tags.

fields.name: rangerTagSyncComponentType
fields.label: Ranger component type
fields.help: Leave 'trino' unless connecting a non-Trino tag source.

fields.name: rangerTagSyncDownloadInterval
fields.label: Sync interval (ms)
fields.help: Default 230s. Lower → tags propagate faster, more load on OM.

fields.name: rangerTagSyncBatchSize
fields.label: Batch size (entities/page)
fields.help: Default 10000. Raise for catalogs >100k entities.

fields.name: postgresql.storage.size
fields.label: PostgreSQL — PVC Size
fields.help: Persistent volume size for the PostgreSQL database. Increase for large metadata graphs.

fields.name: postgresql.storage.storageClass
fields.label: PostgreSQL — StorageClass
fields.help: Leave empty to use the cluster default StorageClass.

fields.name: opensearch.storage.size
fields.label: OpenSearch — PVC Size
fields.help: Persistent volume size for the OpenSearch index.

fields.name: opensearch.storage.storageClass
fields.label: OpenSearch — StorageClass
fields.help: Leave empty to use the cluster default StorageClass.

fields.name: replicaCount
fields.label: Replicas
fields.help: Scale to ≥ 2 with sticky sessions enabled on the Ingress for HA.

fields.name: monitoring.discovery
fields.label: Discover monitoring stack
fields.help: Finds the Prometheus already on the cluster and fills the fields below.

fields.name: monitoring.namespace
fields.label: Monitoring namespace
fields.help: Where the Prometheus stack runs. The ServiceMonitor itself is always created in the release namespace.

fields.name: monitoring.release
fields.label: Monitoring release (Helm)
fields.help: Helm release of the kube-prometheus-stack that should scrape OpenMetadata. Set as the 'release' label of the ServiceMonitor.

fields.name: monitoring.serviceMonitorLabels
fields.label: ServiceMonitor labels
fields.help: Labels the Prometheus selects ServiceMonitors by, as key=value pairs separated by commas. Filled by discovery.

fields.name: ingress.enabled
fields.label: Enable Ingress
fields.help: Expose the service through an Ingress (a Route on OpenShift).
fields.helpMore: Required with an authentication profile (OIDC, LDAP over TLS): sign-in needs a public hostname and HTTPS.

fields.name: ingress.ingressClassName
fields.label: Ingress class
fields.help: Ingress class, e.g. nginx. Blank: the default controller.
fields.helpMore: Hidden on OpenShift, where Routes handle the traffic.

fields.name: ingress.host
fields.label: Hostname (DNS)
fields.help: Public DNS name the ingress controller will route. e.g. service.example.com.

fields.name: ingress.path
fields.label: HTTP path
fields.help: Base path for the Ingress (usually '/').

fields.name: ingress.tlsMode
fields.label: TLS mode
fields.help: Where the service's TLS certificate comes from.
fields.helpMore:
Sign via cert-manager: recommended when cert-manager is installed (renews automatically).
Sign with Company CA: a CA uploaded under Security → Certificate Authorities.
Sign with Ambari Internal CA: for tests, browsers warn.
Modes whose system is not installed are hidden. TLS is required with an authentication profile.
On Upgrade/Config this starts on 'Keep current certificate' (or 'None' for plain HTTP). Pick another mode only to replace the certificate; you are asked to confirm, and a Secret kept by cert-manager or an external store is never overwritten.

options.label: Source from external Secret store (Vault, ESO)
None (HTTP only — not allowed with auth)

fields.name: ingress.tlsSecret
fields.label: Existing TLS Secret name
fields.help: Name of a kubernetes.io/tls Secret already present in the release namespace. The chart references it via ingress.tls[].secretName.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.cert
fields.label: TLS certificate (PEM, leaf + chain)
fields.help: Paste the full chain (leaf first). Saved as tls.crt in the new Secret.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.key
fields.label: TLS private key (PEM)
fields.help: Paste the private key matching the certificate above. Saved as tls.key.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.secretName
fields.label: Target Secret name
fields.help: Secret created from the uploaded certificate. Blank: <release>-ingress-tls.

fields.name: ingress.tlsSelfSign.caName
fields.label: Company CA
fields.help: Company CA that signs the service's certificate.
fields.helpMore: KDPS signs the certificate itself: the CA key never goes to the release's cluster. Upload CAs under Security → Certificate Authorities.

fields.name: ingress.tlsSelfSign.validityDays
fields.label: Leaf validity (days)
fields.help: How long the minted leaf certificate is valid. Capped server-side at 825 (CA/Browser Forum baseline).

fields.name: ingress.certManager.issuerName
fields.label: ClusterIssuer
fields.help: cert-manager issuer that signs and renews the certificate.
fields.helpMore: KDPS writes a Certificate before the install; cert-manager creates the Secret and renews it before it expires.

fields.name: ingress.certManager.validityDays
fields.label: Leaf validity (days)
fields.help: Validity in days. Translated to durationHours on the Certificate resource. cert-manager renews at duration/6 before expiry.

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.secretStoreName
fields.label: SecretStore
fields.help: Pick an external-secrets SecretStore or ClusterSecretStore. Typically Vault-backed for TLS leaves (PKI mount).

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.remoteKey
fields.label: Remote key / path
fields.help: Path of the certificate in the external store.
fields.helpMore: Vault PKI: pki/issue/<role>. Vault KV: secret/data/tls/<name>. AWS Secrets Manager: the secret's name.

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.refreshInterval
fields.label: Refresh interval
fields.help: ESO refresh cadence. e.g. '1h', '15m', '0' (no periodic refresh).

fields.name: ingress.route.ipWhitelist
fields.label: Allowed source IPs (OpenShift Route)
fields.help: Source IPs or CIDRs allowed to reach the Route, space separated. Blank: all.
fields.helpMore: OpenShift only, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8 172.16.20.0/24. Set it when the cluster requires the haproxy.router.openshift.io/ip_whitelist annotation on every Route.

fields.name: ingressTuning
fields.label: Ingress tuning (nginx)

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBufferSize
fields.label: proxy-buffer-size
fields.help: nginx proxy-buffer-size. Blank: the chart's default.
fields.helpMore: 16k under OIDC, else nginx's default (4k/8k). Raise it on 502 'upstream sent too big header' after sign-in.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBuffersNumber
fields.label: proxy-buffers-number
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffers-number. Total response buffers = number × size.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBusyBuffersSize
fields.label: proxy-busy-buffers-size
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-busy-buffers-size. Should be ≥ proxy-buffer-size and ≤ total buffer capacity.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBodySize
fields.label: proxy-body-size
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size. Maximum request body the proxy accepts (e.g. '64m'). Bump for large uploads / file imports.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyReadTimeout
fields.label: proxy-read-timeout (seconds)
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout. Bump for long-running queries (Trino, Superset). Default 60.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyConnectTimeout
fields.label: proxy-connect-timeout (seconds)
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-connect-timeout. Time the proxy waits when opening a connection to the backend pod.
Advanced nginx settings: usually leave blank.
fields.helpMore: Override them for large OAuth headers, long-running queries or big uploads.

fields.name: tls.https.enabled
fields.label: Enable internal HTTPS
fields.help: Enables server-side TLS on the OpenMetadata API port. Ambari auto-generates a PKCS12 keystore signed by the internal CA.

fields.name: tls.https.secretName
fields.label: Keystore Secret
fields.help: Leave empty → <release>-https.

ranger-tagsync-settings._description: Chart-wide TagSync wiring — mirrors the role of ranger-plugin-settings for the plugin side. Drives planRangerTagSyncSources gating (the registration runs only when the values at enabled_helm_prop are true; otherwise the step only reads ranger-tagsync-site and reports what it finds), the submit-time check that the Airflow at airflow_enabled_helm_prop is deployed and the endpoint at endpoint_helm_prop is set, AND the OM_RANGER_TAGSYNC_REGISTER runtime handler (endpoint helm path, fernet Secret coordinates, bot username). Per-source entries below carry identity-only fields.

ranger-openmetadata-tagsync._description: Per-source identity. Chart-wide wiring lives in ranger-tagsync-settings above.
ranger-openmetadata-tagsync._source_key_note: source_key MUST be 'openmetadatarest' — OpenmetadataRESTTagSource reads its endpoint/token from the fixed prefix ranger.tagsync.source.openmetadatarest.* (see TagSyncConfig). Using the entry name instead yields 'OpenmetadataEndpoint not specified'.

retiredValues._comment: Values an earlier version of this definition wrote, removed from the values of every deploy.
retiredValues.openmetadata-env/OPENMETADATA_ADMIN_USER: The wizard no longer asks for the administrator, which the chart never read.
retiredValues.openmetadata-env/OPENMETADATA_ADMIN_PASS: The wizard no longer asks for an administrator password, which the chart never read: KDPS generates it into the Secret <release>-openmetadata-admin.
retiredValues.openmetadata-env/OPENMETADATA_DB_PASSWOR: The wizard no longer asks for a database password, which the chart never read: KDPS generates it into the Secret <release>-openmetadata-db.

generatedSecrets.comment: Basic authentication (no security profile): OpenMetadata gives its bootstrap administrators the password 'admin'; the chart's Job sets them to this one. resetOnUpgrade is true on every deploy, not only until a deploy succeeds: the chart runs the Job in basic authentication only, and OpenMetadata clears the administrators' passwords while it runs with an OIDC or LDAP profile, then gives them 'admin' again at its first start in basic authentication. The Secret is therefore the one place the password is kept: a password changed in OpenMetadata is set back to it by the next deploy.
generatedSecrets.label: the password of the OpenMetadata administrators
generatedSecrets.notice: Without a security profile (basic authentication), the OpenMetadata administrators sign in with the password in the Secret {{namespace}}/{{secretName}}. Read it with: {{readCommand}}. Each deploy sets it again: to change it, write the new password into the Secret, then deploy again.

generatedSecrets.comment: The bundled PostgreSQL keeps the passwords it was initialized with: a release installed before keeps those its chart stored in <release>-postgresql, or, when an uninstall deleted that Secret, the user password the chart set for every release (openmetadata). OpenMetadata never signs in as postgres: that password is generated when it cannot be found. The Airflow scheduler gets the password as a file: KDPS reads the ingestion-bot token from the database through it (OmBotJwtClient).
generatedSecrets.label: the passwords of the OpenMetadata PostgreSQL database

generatedSecrets.comment: The bundled Airflow's administrator, which the OpenMetadata server deploys pipelines with: the create-user job creates it with this password, or sets it on an existing one, and the server reads the same Secret.
generatedSecrets.label: the password of the bundled Airflow administrator
generatedSecrets.notice: The bundled Airflow's administrator 'admin' has the password in the Secret {{namespace}}/{{secretName}}. Read it with: {{readCommand}}

generatedSecrets.comment: The bundled Airflow's PostgreSQL (fixed name openmetadata-airflow-postgresql) and the connection Airflow opens to it. Like the OpenMetadata database: a release installed before keeps its password, or the chart's former airflow_pass when an uninstall deleted the chart's Secret.
generatedSecrets.label: the passwords of the bundled Airflow PostgreSQL database

hive.label: Federated ingestion (external Kerberos keytab)
hive.comment: Safe gate (Trino pattern): the external path triggers ONLY when the operator uploads a keytab Secret via hive.externalKeytabSecret — a MANAGED same-realm deploy leaves it blank and keeps auto-minting, so no regression on k8s target clusters. When set, the applyTo repoints global.security.kerberos.keytab.* (consumed by the OM server, native ingestion AND — via the chart's tpl'd airflow volume — the KubernetesExecutor ingestion task pods) at the uploaded Secret, and deployUsesExternalKeytab() skips the Ambari mint (a backend-realm principal is not issuable by the hosting KDC). The ingestion pods auto-detect the principal from the keytab (klist), so no principal override is needed; the uploaded Secret must carry key 'service.keytab'. This one keytab covers every federated service the ingestion reaches (Hive, Atlas, HDFS).

securityCoupling.unauthenticatedExposure: OpenMetadata then uses basic authentication with its local accounts only: its administrators sign in with the password KDPS keeps in a Secret, and your directory and single sign-on are not used.

baseIngestionHive._description: Marker — presence tells CommandService.submitDeploy to queue OM_HIVE_BASE_INGESTION_REGISTER (before Atlas federation) when baseIngestion.hiveEnabled=true. The step reads Hive connection params from the materialised helm values at execute time.

atlasFederation._description: Marker — presence of this block tells CommandService.submitDeploy to queue the OM_ATLAS_FEDERATION_REGISTER step after the chart installs (only when atlasFederation.enabled=true in form values). The step body reads Atlas connection params from the materialised helm values at execute time.

replayableActions.label: Re-register Ranger TagSync source

warnUnlessValueTrue.message: Ranger TagSync is turned off for this release. Re-registering still adds OpenMetadata as a tag source of the platform's Ranger TagSync (restarting it when its configuration changes), and later deployments of the release will not update that registration. To keep it, turn 'Enable Ranger TagSync' on with Upgrade / Config instead.

replayableActions._description: Reruns the OM→Ranger TagSync source registration. Visible on the release row when service.json declares a ranger-tagsync-source entry. Asks for confirmation when the release has Ranger TagSync turned off.

replayableActions.label: Re-register Atlas federation
replayableActions._description: Replays the four OM REST calls that wire an Atlas federation. Hidden when atlasFederation.enabled=false in the release values so the operator doesn't get a button that always fails.

replayableActions.label: Re-register Hive ingestion
replayableActions._description: Replays the OpenMetadata Hive databaseService + metadata pipeline registration from the deployed values.

replayableActions.label: Re-register Trino ingestion
replayableActions._description: Replays the OpenMetadata Trino databaseService + metadata pipeline registration (and the kdps metadata grants) from the deployed values.

sizing._comment: Sizes offered at step 3 of the wizard. A size fills the listed form fields; M is the fields' defaults. The fields are edited in the sizing dialog instead of the form.

gitOpsSecretReferences._comment: A GitOps profile commits the values to Git: each secret goes to a Secret of the release namespace, which the values name (StackServiceDef.gitOpsSecretReferences). The Hive ingestion password is read by KDPS's own step, never by the chart.

gitOpsSecretReferences.label: the security profile's bind password or OIDC client secret
